reading.a: A large orange sun sits behind a two-level road bridge at dusk: a thin dark powerline crosses the sky and the sun about 100 px above the deck (rows 149-175, falling slightly to the right), the dark deck (element 16) and the truss under it (element 29), the red glow of the sky around the sun (elements 1, 5, 10, 12) and an orange reflection column on dark water (element 36).
reading.b: The Andromeda galaxy: an orange core at (960, 521) in a disk tilted down to the right (element 1, the galaxy's glow), a dense bright gas blob at the core's centre, a dark dust lane below-left of the core, a star field, and one straight satellite streak at about -19 degrees passing 60 px below the core.

concepts.idea: The camera pulls back as in round 11 (0-3.0 s) while, in this order and with every move starting and ending smoothly: the red glow around the sun turns toward the galaxy's colour from the first frame (t 0-0.6, 0-1.8 s), the brightest stars come through the sky (from t 0.08, 0.24 s), the powerline swings 19 degrees and stretches into the satellite streak (t 0.12-0.70, 0.36-2.1 s), the whole sun shrinks fast onto the galaxy's small dense core and takes the core's oval shape and centre, half its radius gone by about t 0.38 (1.1 s), then dissolves into that core's gas from about t 0.51 to 0.82 (1.5-2.5 s) and ends at the last frame (t 0.15-1.0), the bridge folds into the dusty arm in one smooth move (t 0.20-0.85, 0.6-2.55 s), A's sky closes in a circle around the sun (t 0.25-0.92), and the core takes over the last of A brightest-first (t 0.72-1.0, 2.16-3.0 s).

anchors.how: The sun's fitted centre (about (994, 102), radius about 275 px) lands on the core measured as B's bright disc inside the box (measured by the planner on B's 1920 x 1080 canvas: centre (960.0, 520.6), radius 28.2 px, 0.4 px from round 11's typed point), not on a typed point; the camera's scale stays end_scale 0.4.
Unchanged from rounds 9-11: the powerline is A's one thin dark straight line; the streak is B's one thin bright straight line.
Unchanged from rounds 9-11: deck and truss together are the bridge's dark mass; the dust lane is the darkest wide band under the core.

transforms.name: glow_to_galaxy_colour
transforms.note: The lead, not a beat; unchanged from round 11 (he named no fault in the sky's colour).

transforms.name: sun_recedes
transforms.note: Beat 1. Answers 'i would expect whole sun to rapidly shrink at the very small core of galaxy': profile geometric (a constant relative rate, which reads as accelerating into the target), rate fast_in and a sharper start (edge 0.2 instead of the concept's 0.35); computed from the renderer's curves with an end scale of about 0.16 (the planner's estimate from the blob's size), the disc keeps 0.72 of its radius at t 0.30, 0.32 at t 0.50 and 0.24 at t 0.60. Answers 'so the do not align (perfectly ) neither by the centers nor by shapes': end_shape b_blob ends the disc on B's bright blob by its centroid, two axes and angle; blob_frac 0.85 picks the dense core (measured by the planner at 1920 px: centre (959.7, 520.8), axes 18.8 x 16.2 px, 945 px of area; 0.7 picked the 68 x 56 px gas around it, 0.8 a 31 x 26 px blob larger than round 11's end radius 25). Answers 'it should shrink and dissolve into that dense gas': the mix runs on the beat's progress after the rate, so mix_window [0.65, 0.98] places the dissolve at about t 0.51-0.82, after most of the shrink. Answers 'sun limb still is not fully uniform': limb_flatten 0.4 and rim_in 0.5, a guess (0.55 did not level the limb; no render of 0.4 exists). The window ends at 1.0 so the last beat ends at the last frame. reveal_ahead true is the director's intention and the recede's default, written out: the ring the shrinking sun vacates shows the core's glow, because any fill of a luminary's footprint is a dark ring (T46).

transforms.name: wire_to_streak
transforms.note: Beat 2, his round-8 idea, window unchanged. Answers 'elements ( ... ) move a bit discretely': under the motion model the swing starts and ends on the smooth trapezoid (edge 0.35) instead of the smootherstep, and it overlaps the sun's and the bridge's beats. Guarded: B's streak cannot show before the line delivers it.

transforms.name: bridge_to_arm
transforms.note: Beat 3, kept from rounds 8-11 ('bridge trasforms into arm , nice'). Answers 'elements ( especially bridge move a bit discretely (same base issue with linear animation ...)': edge 0.5 makes the bridge's move one smooth hump with no constant-speed part, the softest start and end the motion model gives. Guarded: B's dust lane cannot show before the bridge delivers it.

knobs.name: sun_recedes.params.blob_frac
knobs.what: Which of B's core blobs the sun lands on: 0.8 a 31 x 26 px blob, 0.85 the 19 x 16 px dense core, 0.9 a 10 x 8 px point (measured at 1920 px); higher is smaller and denser.

knobs.name: sun_recedes.params.limb_flatten
knobs.what: How far the sun's limb is levelled toward its centre colour; lower levels more; 0.55 was round 11's value and left the limb uneven.

knobs.name: bridge_to_arm.params.edge
knobs.what: The share of the bridge's window spent speeding up and slowing down; 0.5 is one smooth hump, 0.35 the concept's default with a constant-speed middle.

concepts.risk: Rule 4 (shape alignment): the blob at blob_frac 0.85 is measured on B alone; if the disc lands on it while the camera has not finished its pull-back, the oval can sit off the core in the frame until the last frames; look at end_blob in info.json and at t 0.6-0.9. Rule 5 (no edge in neither photo): limb_flatten 0.4 and rim_in 0.5 are a guess and may draw a paler inner disc (round 9's fault) instead of an even limb; the guard keeps A's base inside the grown streak line and the dust-lane band until each beat arrives, so the sky key can leave a band-shaped edge of A's sky there; read residual_edge_max and look at t 0.3-0.8 around the dust lane and the streak. Rule 11 (rate): fast_in with geometric and edge 0.2 is computed, not seen; the sun barely moves before t 0.25 and may read as a late jump at t 0.3-0.45 rather than a rapid shrink; read motion_jumps. Rule 2: the stars, the key and the colour lead are not beats and keep their own curves. F3 invention: none; every pixel comes from A or B.
